title: C2/C8 prefill is device-bound; longer solo slice rejected

host.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI MAX+ 395 w/ Radeon 8060S

profile_method.protocol: frozen ten-prompt server benchmark, widths 2 and 8 separately, ar_exact, max_tokens=1
profile_method.window_clock: time.perf_counter_ns / CLOCK_MONOTONIC, same nanosecond domain as rocprof kernel timestamps
profile_method.note: This ROCm build did not emit marker CSV output despite confirmed ROCTX callbacks, so kernel rows were sliced by directly recorded prefill start/end timestamps. No compiler ran inside rocprofv3.

c8_prefill_windows.interpretation: some C8 arms execute C7+C1, but arrival timing and slice A/B show the HTTP solo slice is not the cause

batcher_arrival_spans_ms.method: temporary wrapper around _GenerationBatcher.submit; 22 arms per width including two warmups

solo_slice_ab.candidate: temporary general idle-solo slice 2 ms -> 10 ms; no tracked edit
solo_slice_ab.verdict: rejected: C1/C2 regress for only a 1.0% C8 gain; arrivals already fit within 0.7/3.2 ms

conclusion.named_blocker: fully grouped high-row packed prefill is 98-99% GPU-bound, led by Q4 projection owners (~59-60% of GPU sum), with Q6 planar second
conclusion.next: screen existing Q4/Q5/Q6 owners at representative rows96-536 before extending exact selector bands or designing a new high-M owner

correctness.profile_runs: C2 and C8 server artifacts passed all exact/route/budget cells
correctness.slice_ab: C1/C2/C8 candidate passed all 30 exact/route/budget cells
correctness.anti_gaming: full ten-prompt protocol; no token IDs, prompt branches, or exact prompt-row policy
